title: Use a hybrid WordPress product admin instead of a separate app shell
summary: The plugin admin should read as a professional wp-admin extension with a product workflow, not as a custom SaaS interface pasted into WordPress. Filter Presets should make the Theme Builder/Elementor handoff visible during preset creation, while advanced runtime options stay available behind a single deliberate disclosure.
rationale: Visual QA and user feedback showed that the current admin mixes incompatible design signals: WordPress chrome, custom app cards, colored chips, and scattered advanced controls. This makes the intent of each action harder to understand. The product direction still needs a backend admin because reusable presets and CPT definitions belong in WordPress, but the admin must complement Elementor instead of pretending to replace it.
alternatives_considered: Make the admin look completely native to WordPress
Keep the current custom operational shell and only edit copy
Remove the admin UI and put everything into Elementor widgets
Build a full custom visual filter builder inside wp-admin
evidence: Current screenshot audit for TASK-017 captured Dashboard, Filter Presets, Post Types, and Diagnostics pages before changes.

Generated concept image docs/assets/implementation-toolkit/admin-v0.2/concepts/hybrid-wp-admin-filter-preset.png established a compact hybrid direction with Theme Builder handoff first and advanced options collapsed.
Simple Budget Plugin reference shows that plugin-owned Elementor templates are an effective bridge between backend configuration and Elementor visual editing.
risks: Calling the bridge Theme Builder can overpromise Elementor Pro condition integration if the UI does not clarify that it creates/open Elementor templates.
Hiding advanced controls can frustrate power users if the disclosure is not obvious and persistent enough.
CSS changes can improve coherence but still need screenshot validation across all existing admin pages.
